title: Data model checks
description: Adds the check task, to run before a pull request: it starts compose.yaml's Cube in production mode without a data source connection, compiles the model, and compares the SQL Cube generates for each golden query in tests/queries with the snapshot beside it, writing the snapshots in the project's own dialect on the first run and on --update. README.md and AGENTS.md gain the rule that it passes before every pull request.

context_before: - Project-scoped servers are declared in `.mcp.json` (Claude Code), `.codex/config.toml` (Codex, trusted projects only) and `.omp/mcp.json` (oh-my-pi). The three files list the same servers; change all three together.

- Only definitions are committed. Each person authorises the servers themselves: with their own account through OAuth, or with a token they export in the environment variable the server's entry names. No token or credential belongs in these files.
added: - The data model is YAML in `cube/model`: private cubes in `cube/model/cubes`, and the views clients query in `cube/model/views`, as https://docs.cube.dev/recipes/data-modeling/style-guide recommends.
- Settings that differ between environments are `CUBEJS_*` environment variables, never code in `cube/cube.py`. `.env` holds the local ones and is never committed.

- `mise run check` passes before every pull request. When it reports that the SQL of a golden query changed, make sure the change is intended, then run `mise run check --update` and commit the snapshots with the change that caused them.
- A metric that a dashboard or an application depends on gets a golden query in `tests/queries`, with absolute date ranges.

context_before: - the Playground, to build queries and read the SQL they generate, at http://localhost:4000;
- the SQL API, for BI tools, on `localhost:15432`, with any user name and password.
added: `mise run check` starts the Cube image the project pins, in production mode and without connecting to the data source, compiles the model, and checks the golden queries in `tests/queries`. Each `.json` file there is a query a dashboard or an application depends on, and the `.sql` file beside it is the SQL Cube generates for it. The check fails when the model does not compile, when a query asks for a member that no longer exists, or when the SQL of a query changes.

After an intended change, `mise run check --update` rewrites the snapshots, so the pull request shows reviewers how the SQL behind each metric changes. Give every metric something depends on a golden query, with absolute date ranges so its SQL stays the same from day to day.

content: //MISE description="Compile the data model and compare the SQL of every golden query with its snapshot"
// Starts a one-off copy of compose.yaml's cube service in production mode,
// which never connects to the data source. It compiles the model through
// /cubejs-api/v1/meta, then asks /cubejs-api/v1/sql for the SQL of every query
// in tests/queries/*.json and compares it with the .sql snapshot beside it.
//   mise run check            fail when the model does not compile, a query no
//                             longer resolves, or the SQL of a query changed
//   mise run check --update   rewrite the snapshots after an intended change
// Golden queries are the queries clients depend on: renaming or removing a
// member one of them uses fails the check, and the snapshot diff in a pull
// request shows how the SQL behind each metric changes. Give them absolute
// date ranges, so their SQL stays the same from one day to the next.
import { existsSync, mkdtempSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
const unsigned = `${encode({ alg: "HS256", typ: "JWT" })}.${encode({ iat: now, exp: now + 3600 })}`;
const lines = [`-- SQL of ${file}, written by mise run check. Update it with mise run check --update.`];
// diff exits 1 when the files differ, which is the case here.
// Production mode, so the check compiles the model as deployments do, with an
// in-memory queue instead of Cube Store, since nothing here runs a query.
return { status: response.status, body: { error: text } };
throw new Error("Cube did not start; its last log lines are above.");
throw new Error(`The data model does not compile:\n${meta.body.error ?? JSON.stringify(meta.body)}`);
console.log(`✓ the data model compiles: ${views} views, ${members.length - views} public cubes`);
if (!files.length) console.log(`  no golden queries in ${QUERIES}/*.json`);
const { status, body } = await request("sql", { query });
if (process.env.GITHUB_ACTIONS) console.log(`::warning file=${path}::No snapshot was committed for ${file}`);
console.log(`✗ ${file}: its SQL changed. If the change is intended, run mise run check --update and commit the snapshot.`);
